stimulus:
A noiseless patient spider,
I mark'd where on a little promontory it stood isolated,
Mark'd how to explore the vacant vast surrounding,
It launch'd forth filament, filament, filament, out of itself,
Ever unreeling them, ever tirelessly speeding them.

And you O my soul where you stand,
Surrounded, detached, in measureless oceans of space,
Ceaselessly musing, venturing, throwing, seeking the spheres to connect them,
Till the bridge you will need be form'd, till the ductile anchor hold,
Till the gossamer thread you fling catch somewhere, O my soul.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Chromatin persistence after stimulus washout (the anchor test)
ideas.description: Pulse cells with a transient AP-1 stimulus (e.g., TPA or EGF), then track AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for Fos/Jun), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and H3K27ac at each time point after withdrawal. Memory requires the accessibility or enhancer marks to outlast AP-1 binding, just as the spider's thread needs an anchor to hold after it is flung out.

ideas.title: Degron-mediated AP-1 removal during the quiescent interval
ideas.description: Prime cells with a first stimulus, then use an auxin-inducible or dTAG degron to deplete Fos or Jun during the rest period before a second stimulus. If the faster or stronger re-induction of target genes disappears only when AP-1 is removed in the gap, AP-1 is necessary to carry the memory, not just to read it out.

ideas.title: Savings assay with enhancer motif mutants
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base editing or prime editing to disrupt individual TRE/AP-1 motifs at primed enhancers, then compare primary and secondary responses of nearby genes in wild-type and mutant clones. A memory mechanism predicts that losing a specific motif selectively abolishes the faster secondary response while leaving the first response intact, like a gossamer thread that no longer catches.

ideas.title: Heritability of AP-1 state through mitosis
ideas.description: Use a knock-in Fos or Jun live reporter with lineage tracking to sort cells by prior AP-1 history and follow them through several divisions, then test whether daughter cells retain the primed response. Live imaging of chromatin binding during mitosis (mitotic bookmarking) will show whether AP-1 stays bound across division, which would make the memory cell-heritable.

ideas.title: Single-molecule residence time versus memory duration
ideas.description: Measure the chromatin residence time of AP-1 subunits by single-molecule tracking or FRAP in live cells, and pair it with pulse-chase protein half-life measurements (SNAP/HaloTag). Test whether a longer-lived or more stably bound AP-1 population predicts how long the memory lasts across perturbations such as cycloheximide or stabilizing mutants, like the filament that keeps unreeling until it finds a place to hold.
